title: CryoAtlas: A Large Curated Dataset and Unified Benchmark for Cryo-EM Atomic Model Building
claim: A new benchmark is defined by its task, curation pipeline, and unified multi-metric, stratified evaluation protocol.
layout: 3 stacked labeled panels (A–C), left-to-right flow, color-coded metric boxes
description: Three stacked rounded panels labeled A, B and C. Panel A shows the task. A purple cryo-EM density map and a rainbow protein sequence feed an 'Automated model building' box. The box splits into Traditional steps (trace chains, assign residues, place atoms, fit density) and Neural steps (CNN segment, GNN refine, post-process). An arrow leads to the atomic model. A dashed inset shows sequence-only prediction. Panel B is a left-to-right flow. EMDB and PDB database icons lead to 24,052 candidates, then an alignment and QC gear, then 17,809 curated records. These split into 16,657 training and 1,152 test, and the test set passes through three funnel filters to a 618 common benchmark. Panel C has three colored boxes for the metric groups (stereochemical, structural accuracy, model-map fitness), each with a molecule image and metric names. Below them is a row of four stratified-analysis chips: resolution, length, train-test similarity and protein category.
caption: Overview of CryoAtlas. A. Task definition: cryo-EM model building uses density maps and protein sequences to produce a map-aligned atomic model, whereas sequence-based prediction uses sequence alone. B. Dataset curation workflow, resulting in 16,657 training targets and 1,152 test targets; methods are benchmarked on a shared 618-target subset. C. CryoAtlas evaluates different methods using new composite metrics and performs stratified analysis across four factors.
abstract: Deep learning has accelerated automated atomic model building from cryo-EM maps, yet progress remains limited by the lack of large, high-quality datasets and standardized evaluation benchmarks. We address this gap by introducing CryoAtlas, a rigorously curated dataset and unified benchmark for density-guided atomic model building of protein chains. By integrating and filtering EMDB and PDB entries (up to March 2026), CryoAtlas provides 17,809 map-model-sequence entries, including a curated 16,657-entry training split. From this resource, we construct a 618-target benchmark with a shared evaluation protocol that jointly assesses structural accuracy, model-to-map fit, and stereochemical validity. Using this framework, we benchmark state-of-the-art learning-based methods against Phenix and AlphaFold3, comprehensively analyzing the impact of map resolution, sequence length, protein category and sequence identity on modeling accuracy. As a case study, retraining the ModelAngelo CNN component on CryoAtlas improves performance on the benchmark. CryoAtlas provides an open, reproducible foundation for future cryo-EM atomic model building research. Project details and resource release updates are available at https://oulling.github.io/cryoatlas/.
